content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_axi_pr293, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# axi_pkg::LenWidth not compatible with vivado IP packager
Since commit [fe4e020](https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/commit/fe4e020f2c06a242d4901b23cedbf2eeab22bfe6) the typedef`axi_pkg::burst_t` now relies on a Verilog parameter `BurstWidth`.
https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/blob/fd60be8b51a4fa7476856be162ce3334474592ba/src/axi_pkg.sv#L46
In [Occamy emulation](https://github.com/pulp-platform/snitch/blob/master/hw/system/occamy/src/occamy_xilinx.sv) we use these typedefs at the ports of a custom packaged Vivado IP.
But Vivado requires that "the IP ports are contained within the port description of the HDL file" (c.f. [doc](https://www.xilinx.com/support/documents/sw_manuals/xilinx2022_1/ug1118-vivado-creating-packaging-custom-ip.pdf) page 14).
So custom Vivado IPs can't use `axi_pkg::burst_t` at their top anymore (similar issue on this [support thread](https://support.xilinx.com/s/question/0D52E00006hpfh5SAA/ipflow-19627-hdl-parameter-fpgamanu-fpga-manu-xpath-expression-failed-undefined-parameter-xilinx-used-in-expression-xilinx?language=en_US))
We could maybe define the typdef with a numerical value and then the parameter based on the `$size` of this typedef.
See proposition in  https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/commit/d2f98d691594c1a8dd1af5bedd5d37d965027535

Here is the project file that may be relevant to this issue:

67   /// In a fixed burst:
68   /// - The address is the same for every transfer in the burst.
69   /// - The byte lanes that are valid are constant for all beats in the burst.  However, within
70   ///   those byte lanes, the actual bytes that have `wstrb` asserted can differ for each beat in
71   ///   the burst.
72   /// This burst type is used for repeated accesses to the same location such as when loading or
73   /// emptying a FIFO.
74   localparam BURST_FIXED = 2'b00;
75   /// In an incrementing burst, the address for each transfer in the burst is an increment of the
76   /// address for the previous transfer.  The increment value depends on the size of the transfer.
77   /// For example, the address for each transfer in a burst with a size of 4 bytes is the previous
78   /// address plus four.
79   /// This burst type is used for accesses to normal sequential memory.
80   localparam BURST_INCR  = 2'b01;
81   /// A wrapping burst is similar to an incrementing burst, except that the address wraps around to
82   /// a lower address if an upper address limit is reached.
83   /// The following restrictions apply to wrapping bursts:
84   /// - The start address must be aligned to the size of each transfer.
85   /// - The length of the burst must be 2, 4, 8, or 16 transfers.
86   localparam BURST_WRAP  = 2'b10;
87 
88   /// Normal access success.  Indicates that a normal access has been successful. Can also indicate
89   /// that an exclusive access has failed.
90   localparam RESP_OKAY   = 2'b00;
91   /// Exclusive access okay.  Indicates that either the read or write portion of an exclusive access
92   /// has been successful.
93   localparam RESP_EXOKAY = 2'b01;
94   /// Slave error.  Used when the access has reached the slave successfully, but the slave wishes to
95   /// return an error condition to the originating master.
96   localparam RESP_SLVERR = 2'b10;
97   /// Decode error.  Generated, typically by an interconnect component, to indicate that there is no
98   /// slave at the transaction address.
99   localparam RESP_DECERR = 2'b11;
100 
101   /// When this bit is asserted, the interconnect, or any component, can delay the transaction
102   /// reaching its final destination for any number of cycles.

104   /// When HIGH, Modifiable indicates that the characteristics of the transaction can be modified.

114   /// Maximum number of bytes per burst, as specified by `size` (see Table A3-2).
115   function automatic shortint unsigned num_bytes(size_t size);
116     return 1 << size;
117   endfunction

119   /// An overly long address type.
120   /// It lets us define functions that work generically for shorter addresses.  We rely on the
121   /// synthesizer to optimize the unused bits away.
122   typedef logic [127:0] largest_addr_t;

124   /// Aligned address of burst (see A3-51).
125   function automatic largest_addr_t aligned_addr(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size);
126     return (addr >> size) << size;
127   endfunction

129   /// Warp boundary of a `BURST_WRAP` transfer (see A3-51).
130   /// This is the lowest address accessed within a wrapping burst.
131   /// This address is aligned to the size and length of the burst.
132   /// The length of a `BURST_WRAP` has to be 2, 4, 8, or 16 transfers.
133   function automatic largest_addr_t wrap_boundary (largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len);
134     largest_addr_t wrap_addr;
135 
136     // pragma translate_off
137     `ifndef VERILATOR
138       assume (len == len_t'(4'b1) || len == len_t'(4'b11) || len == len_t'(4'b111) ||
139           len == len_t'(4'b1111)) else
140         $error("AXI BURST_WRAP with not allowed len of: %0h", len);
141     `endif
142     // pragma translate_on
143 
144     // In A3-51 the wrap boundary is defined as:
145     // `Wrap_Boundary = (INT(Start_Address / (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length))) ×
146     //    (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length)`
147     // Whereas the aligned address is defined as:
148     // `Aligned_Address = (INT(Start_Address / Number_Bytes)) × Number_Bytes`
149     // This leads to the wrap boundary using the same calculation as the aligned address, difference
150     // being the additional dependency on the burst length. The addition in the case statement
151     // is equal to the multiplication with `Burst_Length` as a shift (used by `aligned_addr`) is
152     // equivalent with multiplication and division by a power of two, which conveniently are the
153     // only allowed values for `len` of a `BURST_WRAP`.
154     unique case (len)
155       4'b1    : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 1)) << (unsigned'(size) + 1); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `2`
156       4'b11   : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 2)) << (unsigned'(size) + 2); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `4`
157       4'b111  : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 3)) << (unsigned'(size) + 3); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `8`
158       4'b1111 : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 4)) << (unsigned'(size) + 4); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `16`
159       default : wrap_addr = '0;
160     endcase
161     return wrap_addr;
162   endfunction
163 
164   /// Address of beat (see A3-51).
165   function automatic largest_addr_t
166   beat_addr(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst, shortint unsigned i_beat);
167     largest_addr_t ret_addr = addr;
168     largest_addr_t wrp_bond = '0;
169     if (burst == BURST_WRAP) begin
170       // do not trigger the function if there is no wrapping burst, to prevent assumptions firing
171       wrp_bond = wrap_boundary(addr, size, len);
172     end
173     if (i_beat != 0 && burst != BURST_FIXED) begin
174       // From A3-51:
175       // For an INCR burst, and for a WRAP burst for which the address has not wrapped, this
176       // equation determines the address of any transfer after the first transfer in a burst:
177       // `Address_N = Aligned_Address + (N – 1) × Number_Bytes` (N counts from 1 to len!)
178       ret_addr = aligned_addr(addr, size) + i_beat * num_bytes(size);
179       // From A3-51:
180       // For a WRAP burst, if Address_N = Wrap_Boundary + (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length), then:
181       // * Use this equation for the current transfer:
182       //     `Address_N = Wrap_Boundary`
183       // * Use this equation for any subsequent transfers:
184       //     `Address_N = Start_Address + ((N – 1) × Number_Bytes) – (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length)`
185       // This means that the address calculation of a `BURST_WRAP` fundamentally works the same
186       // as for a `BURST_INC`, the difference is when the calculated address increments
187       // over the wrap threshold, the address wraps around by subtracting the accessed address
188       // space from the normal `BURST_INCR` address. The lower wrap boundary is equivalent to
189       // The wrap trigger condition minus the container size (`num_bytes(size) * (len + 1)`).
190       if (burst == BURST_WRAP && ret_addr >= wrp_bond + (num_bytes(size) * (len + 1))) begin
191         ret_addr = ret_addr - (num_bytes(size) * (len + 1));
192       end
193     end
194     return ret_addr;
195   endfunction
196 
197   /// Index of lowest byte in beat (see A3-51).
198   function automatic shortint unsigned
199   beat_lower_byte(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst,
200       shortint unsigned strobe_width, shortint unsigned i_beat);
201     largest_addr_t _addr = beat_addr(addr, size, len, burst, i_beat);
202     return shortint'(_addr - (_addr / strobe_width) * strobe_width);
203   endfunction
204 
205   /// Index of highest byte in beat (see A3-51).
206   function automatic shortint unsigned
207   beat_upper_byte(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst,
208       shortint unsigned strobe_width, shortint unsigned i_beat);
209     if (i_beat == 0) begin
210       return aligned_addr(addr, size) + (num_bytes(size) - 1) - (addr / strobe_width) * strobe_width;
211     end else begin
212       return beat_lower_byte(addr, size, len, burst, strobe_width, i_beat) + num_bytes(size) - 1;
213     end
214   endfunction

278   /// RESP precedence: DECERR > SLVERR > OKAY > EXOKAY.  This is not defined in the AXI standard but
279   /// depends on the implementation.  We consistently use the precedence above.  Rationale:
280   /// - EXOKAY means an exclusive access was successful, whereas OKAY means it was not.  Thus, if
281   ///   OKAY and EXOKAY are to be merged, OKAY precedes because the exclusive access was not fully
282   ///   successful.
283   /// - Both DECERR and SLVERR mean (part of) a transaction were unsuccessful, whereas OKAY means an
284   ///   entire transaction was successful.  Thus both DECERR and SLVERR precede OKAY.
285   /// - DECERR means (part of) a transactions could not be routed to a slave component, whereas
286   ///   SLVERR means the transaction reached a slave component but lead to an error condition there.
287   ///   Thus DECERR precedes SLVERR because DECERR happens earlier in the handling of a transaction.
288   function automatic resp_t resp_precedence(resp_t resp_a, resp_t resp_b);
289     unique case (resp_a)
290       RESP_OKAY: begin
291         // Any response except EXOKAY precedes OKAY.
292         if (resp_b == RESP_EXOKAY) begin
293           return resp_a;
294         end else begin
295           return resp_b;
296         end
297       end
298       RESP_EXOKAY: begin
299         // Any response precedes EXOKAY.
300         return resp_b;
301       end
302       RESP_SLVERR: begin
303         // Only DECERR precedes SLVERR.
304         if (resp_b == RESP_DECERR) begin
305           return resp_b;
306         end else begin
307           return resp_a;
308         end
309       end
310       RESP_DECERR: begin
311         // No response precedes DECERR.
312         return resp_a;
313       end
314     endcase
315   endfunction

376   // ATOP[5:0]
377   /// - Sends a single data value with an address.
378   /// - The target swaps the value at the addressed location with the data value that is supplied in
379   ///   the transaction.
380   /// - The original data value at the addressed location is returned.
381   /// - Outbound data size is 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes.
382   /// - Inbound data size is the same as the outbound data size.
383   localparam ATOP_ATOMICSWAP  = 6'b110000;
384   /// - Sends two data values, the compare value and the swap value, to the addressed location.
385   ///   The compare and swap values are of equal size.
386   /// - The data value at the addressed location is checked against the compare value:
387   ///   - If the values match, the swap value is written to the addressed location.
388   ///   - If the values do not match, the swap value is not written to the addressed location.
389   /// - The original data value at the addressed location is returned.
390   /// - Outbound data size is 2, 4, 8, 16, or 32 bytes.
391   /// - Inbound data size is half of the outbound data size because the outbound data contains both
392   ///   compare and swap values, whereas the inbound data has only the original data value.
393   localparam ATOP_ATOMICCMP   = 6'b110001;
394   // ATOP[5:4]
395   /// Perform no atomic operation.
396   localparam ATOP_NONE        = 2'b00;
397   /// - Sends a single data value with an address and the atomic operation to be performed.
398   /// - The target performs the operation using the sent data and value at the addressed location as
399   ///   operands.
400   /// - The result is stored in the address location.
401   /// - A single response is given without data.
402   /// - Outbound data size is 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes.
403   localparam ATOP_ATOMICSTORE = 2'b01;
404   /// Sends a single data value with an address and the atomic operation to be performed.
405   /// - The original data value at the addressed location is returned.
406   /// - The target performs the operation using the sent data and value at the addressed location as
407   ///   operands.
408   /// - The result is stored in the address location.
409   /// - Outbound data size is 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes.
410   /// - Inbound data size is the same as the outbound data size.
411   localparam ATOP_ATOMICLOAD  = 2'b10;
412   // ATOP[3]
413   /// For AtomicStore and AtomicLoad transactions `AWATOP[3]` indicates the endianness that is
414   /// required for the atomic operation.  The value of `AWATOP[3]` applies to arithmetic operations
415   /// only and is ignored for bitwise logical operations.
416   /// When deasserted, this bit indicates that the operation is little-endian.
417   localparam ATOP_LITTLE_END  = 1'b0;
418   /// When asserted, this bit indicates that the operation is big-endian.
419   localparam ATOP_BIG_END     = 1'b1;
420   // ATOP[2:0]
421   /// The value in memory is added to the sent data and the result stored in memory.
422   localparam ATOP_ADD   = 3'b000;
423   /// Every set bit in the sent data clears the corresponding bit of the data in memory.
424   localparam ATOP_CLR   = 3'b001;
425   /// Bitwise exclusive OR of the sent data and value in memory.
426   localparam ATOP_EOR   = 3'b010;
427   /// Every set bit in the sent data sets the corresponding bit of the data in memory.
428   localparam ATOP_SET   = 3'b011;
429   /// The value stored in memory is the maximum of the existing value and sent data. This operation
430   /// assumes signed data.
431   localparam ATOP_SMAX  = 3'b100;
432   /// The value stored in memory is the minimum of the existing value and sent data. This operation
433   /// assumes signed data.
434   localparam ATOP_SMIN  = 3'b101;
435   /// The value stored in memory is the maximum of the existing value and sent data. This operation
436   /// assumes unsigned data.
437   localparam ATOP_UMAX  = 3'b110;
438   /// The value stored in memory is the minimum of the existing value and sent data. This operation
439   /// assumes unsigned data.
440   localparam ATOP_UMIN  = 3'b111;
441   // ATOP[5] == 1'b1 indicated that an atomic transaction has a read response
442   // Ussage eg: if (req_i.aw.atop[axi_pkg::ATOP_R_RESP]) begin
443   localparam ATOP_R_RESP = 32'd5;
444 
445   // `xbar_latency_e` and `xbar_cfg_t` are documented in `doc/axi_xbar.md`.
446   /// Slice on Demux AW channel.
447   localparam logic [9:0] DemuxAw = (1 << 9);
448   /// Slice on Demux W channel.
449   localparam logic [9:0] DemuxW  = (1 << 8);
450   /// Slice on Demux B channel.
451   localparam logic [9:0] DemuxB  = (1 << 7);
452   /// Slice on Demux AR channel.
453   localparam logic [9:0] DemuxAr = (1 << 6);
454   /// Slice on Demux R channel.
455   localparam logic [9:0] DemuxR  = (1 << 5);
456   /// Slice on Mux AW channel.

458   /// Slice on Mux W channel.
459   localparam logic [9:0] MuxW    = (1 << 3);
460   /// Slice on Mux B channel.
